issue.title: test_full_lifecycle_dismiss_then_revive_named_agent cannot find its initial fixture under the broad lane
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1tc.3.1.6.3 note #1; triaged by sase-1tc.3.1.6.land at primary 5b08952c6d. ToolRun 19d8d493aae60d66655ce12bab0d4a87 failed this node in the parallel scoped lane (26 failures, 9289 passed); its one chop SIGTERM notice-count failure was fixed by the epic and is excluded. The proposing phase recorded all other 25 nodes passing serially on clean base 4e5c1b9730 and its unchanged tree. The lander independently reran all 25 nodes together serially at 5b08952c6d: 25 passed in 16.39s. Observed one broad-run failure and passing serial controls; population failure rate and root cause remain unknown. Do not weaken assertions, raise timeouts, or add baseline entries. Investigate reproducible test isolation/index state first. Size large is intentional because the cause is unproven. All-status flake searches, all-type exact-node searches, and both recent-task sweeps found no semantic duplicate for this scope. Active sase-j7/.4 and sase-zu/.3 were reviewed: thematic overlap, but no demonstrated causal mechanism, so neither receives an ownership claim. Adjacent tracking exists in sase-1oo (claim prepass), sase-1pr (unloaded dismissal), sase-1on (group revival), and sase-1sg (TUI full-history row); they are related, not assumed identical. This is unrelated to chop batch recovery code.

The precondition at line 196 fails: find_named_agent('foo') returns None before dismissal/revival starts. Distinct from sase-1pr (leftover rows after dismissal) and sase-1sg (TUI full-history list); do not assume their root causes match.

Nodes:
- tests/test_dismissed_agent_lifecycle.py::test_full_lifecycle_dismiss_then_revive_named_agent
